description: We are Urban Tech students at Cornell University with backgrounds in AI, technology and architecture. We enjoy building new things, exploring ideas and taking on challenges.
summary:
We developed an SMS-based crop recommendation system that helps farmers decide what to grow, when to plant and harvest, and how to get the most out of their land. Farmers interact in their own language, mark their fields on a simple map and receive recommendations based on 20 years of weather history, soil conditions, satellite imagery and USDA data.

The system evaluates 18 crops, compares rotation strategies, identifies risks such as frost, drought and erosion, and estimates how often each crop could successfully reach harvest. We also built a Harvest ROI feature to compare potential returns across crops and identify the most profitable harvest options for the land.

We kept AI out of the decision-making process: all facts, calculations and recommendations are generated by code, while AI only handles replies and translation. This makes the advice more reliable while keeping it accessible to farmers who may not have access to smartphones, dashboards or technical tools.

Our goal is simple: help farmers make better decisions using data they can actually access.
details:
We developed a crop recommendation and rotation planning system that helps farmers understand what to grow on their land and when. The farmer interacts with the system through SMS in their own language, marks their field on a simple map and answers a few questions about their current crops, previous harvests, water availability and priorities.

Using 20 years of historical weather data, soil information, satellite imagery and elevation data, the system evaluates 18 crops and compares different rotation strategies. It looks at factors such as frost, rainfall, soil moisture, heat, crop maturity and erosion to estimate how often a crop could successfully reach harvest. Farmers receive the recommendations, along with planting and harvesting months, potential risks, cover crops and ways to address them.

We also developed a Harvest ROI feature that compares different crop options based on expected yield, production costs and market prices. It estimates which harvest would make the best economic use of the available land. Farmers can also ask when and where to sell their crops and get estimated price ranges and earnings per hectare.

One important design decision was keeping AI away from the actual calculations and recommendations. All numbers, dates, links and advice are generated by our code. AI is only used to understand farmer responses and translate messages. If a translation changes a number, it is rejected and the original message is sent instead. This came from an early test where the model generated a fake map link.

The project is designed for farmers who may not have access to reliable internet, smartphones or technical dashboards. By using SMS and a simple map, we want to make data-driven farming decisions easier to access and use.

Technology used: We built the backend in TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, using the Agents SDK and Durable Objects for farmer sessions, Workers AI (Mistral Small 3.1) for language processing, KV for caching and D1 for market data. Twilio handles SMS, Leaflet is used for field mapping, and Server-Sent Events stream the analysis to the public demo.

The main challenge we considered was balancing crop productivity with soil and water conservation, while accounting for local weather patterns, market conditions, uncertainty and the farmer's own priorities. We also included cross-checks using USDA crop maps, MODIS satellite observations and NOAA weather stations rather than relying on a single data source.

Our aim is to help farmers make better crop and rotation decisions, reduce avoidable losses and get better returns from the land they already have.
